attributes.body:
どんどん (or ドンドン) is one of the countless words in Japanese that represent a particular sound or sensation. These words are known as onomatopoeia (オノマトペ in Japanese). どんどん represents the sound of banging (like on a drum), or the pounding of feet. In this way, it is regularly translated as 'rapidly', or 'quickly'.

Like だんだん, どんどん may be used before almost any phrase.

While どんどん can take the particle と, it is not required. In fact, と is very often omitted from adverbs/onomatopoeic words in Japanese.

Caution

Initially, it can be easy to mix-up どんどん, with だんだん. だんだん is used to express slower changes, and may be thought of as similar to 'steadily', or 'step by step' in English.

Fun Fact

When the と particle is used with onomatopoeic words, it is very similar to one of と's main usages as a quotation marker in Japanese. This means that と has a similar role to words like 'went', or 'goes' in English. For example, In English, we would say:

The door 'goes' BANG with the wind.

However, the door doesn't actually 'go' anywhere. This is similar to what と is doing here.

だんだん and どんどん are similar-sounding adverbs that both describe change over time, but with different nuances. だんだん suggests a slow, step-by-step progression, like 'gradually' or 'bit by bit'. どんどん implies faster, more dynamic change; something happening quickly or in leaps and bounds.

first_relatable.title: だんだん
first_relatable.meaning: Gradually, Little by little, Step by step

second_relatable.title: どんどん
second_relatable.meaning: Progressively, Rapidly increasing, More and more

attributes.body: どんどん and ますます are both adverbs used to describe change over time. どんどん emphasizes rapid progress or sudden development, often in leaps and bounds. ますます focuses on something already in a certain state becoming even more so, and is often used in polite expressions like wishes for continued health or success.

first_relatable.title: どんどん
first_relatable.meaning: Progressively, Rapidly increasing, More and more

second_relatable.title: ますます
second_relatable.meaning: Increasingly, More and more, Decreasingly, Less and less, Keep -ing

attributes.body: どんどん is an adverb that implies rapid or dramatic change, often in leaps and bounds, and is common in everyday speech. In contrast, 一方だ is more formal and used to describe ongoing change that continues beyond the speaker's control. Structurally, 一方だ follows the verb, unlike どんどん, which appears before it.

first_relatable.title: どんどん
first_relatable.meaning: Progressively, Rapidly increasing, More and more

second_relatable.title: 一方だ
second_relatable.meaning: More and more, Continue to, Keep on, -er and -er

attributes.body: どんどん is an adverb that implies rapid or dramatic change, often in leaps and bounds, e.g. どんどん大きくなる 'grow rapidly'. 〜ば〜ほど is a structure that shows proportional change, like 'the more (A), the more (B)' in English. For example, 大きくなればなるほどいい ('The bigger it gets, the better.').
